outcome: Prevalence of abnormal liver transaminases (AST >40 U/L and ALT >40 U/L)
cohort: The study included 30,460 normal pregnant women who delivered at term and 30,460 matched nonpregnant women younger than 45 years.
finding: The ALT level was lower during pregnancy, reaching its nadir in the second half of the third trimester and postpartum day 1, before returning to nonpregnant levels by postpartum days 2-7, whereas the AST level remained unchanged regardless of pregnancy.
